_comment: Coverage ratchet floor. MO-89 (2026-09-16) replaced the never-regenerated bootstrap value (65.23, taken from a pyproject comment) with a floor derived from a REAL measurement: the full suite (14976 passing tests, Windows, `pytest tests/ -n auto --dist=loadgroup --cov=voice_typer`) measured 84.84% total line coverage. The floor is set 4.84 points BELOW that measurement on purpose: the ratchet runs only on the canonical ubuntu x 3.12 leg (.github/workflows/build.yml) while coverage is measured on every OS, and platform-conditional code (windows/ ~4.8% of statements, linux/ ~1.6%, macos/ ~1.1%) cannot be exercised identically everywhere. A 80.0 floor still removes the ~19 points of slack the bootstrap value left, so any real erosion now fails CI. Raise it ONLY on a fresh measurement (scripts/coverage_ratchet_check.py --regenerate); never lower it to accommodate a drop. HISTORICAL NOTE (2026-02-10): the measurement above predates the deletion of the dead `voice_typer/server/recording/_recorder_split.py`, so its per-file statement and file counts no longer describe the tree. The earlier 'ZERO 0%-coverage modules' claim was falsified by that module (an unimported module is necessarily 0%) and has been REMOVED rather than restated; do not reintroduce it without re-measuring. Deleting a 0%-covered module raises the overall percentage, so the 80.0 floor is unchanged and remains valid -- only this prose was stale. This field is HAND-MAINTAINED: --regenerate refreshes _updated/_source but never rewrites it, so review it on every regeneration.
